about.title: Caribou Wilderness
about.extract: The Caribou Wilderness is a federally designated wilderness area created by the Wilderness Act of 1964 and is part of the National Wilderness Preservation System. It is located 60 miles (97 km) east of Redding in the state of California, United States. The Caribou Wilderness comprises 20,546 acres (83.15 km2) and is adjacent to the east side of Lassen Volcanic National Park. Although the park is surrounded by Lassen National Forest, it is managed separately by the National Park Service, whereas the U.S. Forest Service manages the wilderness.

sites.name: Silver Bowl Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $12 per night
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Located near the shores of Silver Lake, near the Caribou Wilderness, Silver Bowl is a developed campground with 18 designated sites. sites.directions: From county road A21, take Silver Lake road until you reach Silver Lake.

sites.name: Echo Lake
sites.about: Echo Lake is a semi-developed, dispersed camping area at the shoreline of Echo Lake near the Caribou Wilderness. A vault toilet is on site, as well as trash recepticals. sites.name: Crater Lake Campground
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $10 per night
sites.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
sites.waterText: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
sites.about: Campground located 7 miles off highway 44. Motor homes and large trailers not recommended due to rough steep road. There are 17 sites at lake, each site has a fire ring and table. Hand pumped water, vault toilets. Fly fishing, canoeing, and float tubing are favorites at Crater Lake. Fall season…
sites.directions: 28.6 miles from Susanville on Highway 44, turn on forest route 32N08 for 7 miles until you reach the campground.
sites.restrictions: No gas motors on lake. Quiet time is 10PM - 8AM. Check in is 1PM and check out is 12PM.
